title: F5 releases emergency patches for critical BIG-IP RCE flaws
content_md: US cybersecurity company F5 warned customers to patch five BIG-IP vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit to trigger denial-of-service (DoS) or gain remote code execution. Tracked as CVE-2026-121805 , CVE-2026-120292 , CVE-2026-120285 , CVE-2026-116953 , and CVE-2026-123637 , these stack-based buffer overflow flaws affect the company's BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) centralized access management proxy solution and the BIG-IP iRules programmable scripting feature. All five security issues are rated critical severity, and unauthenticated threat actors can exploit them to execute arbitrary code remotely on unpatched systems. The company also released engineering hotfixes for a high-severity BIG-IP APM SAML vulnerability ( CVE-2026-126822 ) stemming from an integer underflow (wrap or wraparound) weakness that remote, unauthenticated threat actors can abuse in denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. F5 said it has no mitigation measures for these flaws and advised security teams to install the out-of-band hotfixes released on Wednesday to address them on vulnerable devices. Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver currently tracks more than 177,000 BIG-IP instances and over 14,600 IP addresses with BIG-IP APM fingerprints exposed online. However, there is no information on how many are honeypots or have already been patched against these vulnerabilities.
